messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [INC-2026-114] Elevated latency & RPM for model-family 'chorus-13b' detected. Auto-sculpt triggered: temporary per-model RPM lowered. Indicators: 95th latency 4.2s, error rate 1.8%. Pager to #eng-oncall.

alex_oncall: acknowledging, joining. pulling graph now.

alex_oncall: quick note — surge seems origin from a single tennant pattern + lots of short-chat calls ; KV cache miss rate up 28%.

priya_sre: grabbing topology. are we seeing funcall-related latency?

alex_oncall: yes, function-calling traces show tail spikes on chorus-13b when tool calls are enabled. Fallbacks working but queuing increases.

jordan_platform: I can apply a temporary carve: lower chorus-13b RPM to 60% of normal and disable funcall for that family. propose window 15m then reassess. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maria_prod: Customer impact check — which tenants hit? support-bot please surface top 10 affected customers and any active SLOs in danger.

support-bot: Top affected tenants: acme-ai (15% errors), travelwise (12%), synthlytics (9%). No paid-enterprise SLA breaches detected yet; monitoring alert threshold at 5m sustained >2% errors.

priya_sre: Agreed to jordan's plan. I'll be on the action path. Alex — can you stage a canary config for premium tenants before global change?

alex_oncall: will do. plan: 1) disable funcall on chorus-13b for non-premium 2) set per-model RPM floor to 60% 3) enable short-term cache bypass for premium. Rolling now.

jordan_platform: Running command to alter per-model rate limits:
```
redwoodctl rate set --model chorus-13b --rpm 6000 --scope global --reason "auto-sculpt mitigation"
redwoodctl feature disable --model chorus-13b --feature funcall --scope non-premium
redwoodctl rate set --model chorus-13b --rpm 12000 --scope premium --reason "premium bridge"
```

priya_sre: Commands issued. Observability: creating temporary dashboard with 30s cadence.

alex_oncall: canary applied to premium tenants — traffic looks green for them (latency 95p down to 1.1s). Non-premium shows immediate drop in queue depth.

maria_prod: Notifying support channels and sending customer-facing note to top impacted accounts. Draft: "We've applied a temporary traffic shaping to model chorus-13b to protect latency — premium customers unaffected. We'll update within 30m."

jordan_platform: Confirmed error rate down to 0.4%, 95p latency 1.5s. KV cache hit improving.

priya_sre: Keeping the lower RPM for 20 minutes, then we'll lift to 80% and monitor. If stable for 15m, restore funcall for non-premium.

alex_oncall: Logging mitigation in incident response playbook and tagging runbook step IDs: RB-14 (per-model-reduction), RB-07 (funcall-disable).

maria_prod: Support message sent. No escalations from customers so far.

support-bot: Incident note auto-saved: INC-2026-114 — per-model RPM sculpt + funcall suspend.

priya_sre: Status check in 10m. If any of you see regression, we revert immediately and open capacity request channel.

alex_oncall: +1. Also will capture sampling of affected requests for postmortem.

jordan_platform: After 20m: raising chorus-13b RPM to 80% for non-premium, keep funcall disabled for now.

priya_sre: Observability steady. error rate 0.2%, 95p 1.3s. Moving to monitoring-only.

maria_prod: Moving to incident->postmortem state. Assigning owner: alex_oncall for follow-up, maria_prod for customer comms.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-114 updated: mitigation applied, status -> monitoring, severity -> Sev2, pager cleared.

alex_oncall: quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely sudden tenant burst with heavy funcall workloads causing KV churn and sequencing stalls. Proposed long-term: per-tenant shaping + funcall cost accounting + autoscale buffer for chorus family.

priya_sre: adding to postmortem checklist: include timeline, commands run, customer impact, metrics snapshot, and action items.

maria_prod: I'll draft customer-facing summary doc and flag any customers requesting SLA credit.

support-bot: Closing thread after 2h if no regressions. :white_check_mark:
